locator: §2.1, 'Some theorists who view themselves as emotivists suggest that even the most general terms of moral evaluation have a descriptive meaning rather than just an emotive or non-cognitive meaning (Stevenson 1944, 22'
interpretation: Stevenson's emotivism as the entry reports it: moral terms have emotive meaning (they express and perhaps evoke emotion, §2.1) and also a descriptive meaning. Read as: every moral sentence has some descriptive meaning; what it is is not formalized. Part of the Stevenson theory bundle (#185). Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
